I was just thinking that maybe I should share some of the useful stuff I learned, so here goes.

Pregnancy rage is a thing. Emotions can be all over the place. I was mostly SUUUUPER happy, but I had fits of rage, not sure which trimester. Some women get very suspicious and anxious and second guess everything in their lives, too. Knowing to expect the mood swings allowed me to control them.

Swelling/water retention is super common in the third trimester. Drinking kombucha daily controlled that for me. I didn't drink it for one day and puffed up, then went back to normal when I had some again.

It's normal to generate a ton of heat, especially in the 3rd trimester.

Starting sometime in the 3rd trimester, babies can hear and remember what they heard. Studies have shown that they already prefer their mother's voice, their mother's language, and can recognize vocal patterns such as poems that were read to them in the womb, even when recited by unfamiliar voices. I played the music I planned to use in labor regularly out loud during pregnancy because of this, so my baby would find it familiar and soothing.

Braxton Hicks contractions, the "practice" ones, can be painful or unnoticeable. Sometimes you can see your belly get tight, but not feel it. Totally normal. If you're getting a lot of them in a day, especially painful ones, make sure you empty your bladder and get hydrated and they'll probably calm down.

Real contractions feel like bad period cramps, and they can be localized in your back. If they're focused in your back, your baby's face is likely pointed the wrong direction. There are ways you can position yourself to help them turn to make labor easier.

If you start throwing up in early labor, eating salt can stop it.

If you're going to baby wear, you can use your wrap or ring sling to help support your belly in the third trimester.

We took a Bradley Method birthing class to prepare for a natural home birth, and if you want to do something like that, it runs longer than I expected, so look into it now.

Newborns have never used their lungs before, aside from hiccuping. It takes a while for their breathing to become regular, and you'll hear them take tiny breaks and then gasp until then. Normal, but kind of terrifying.

If you got food aversions, they usually go away after the baby's out.

Your newborn is going to get hungry every time you want to eat. It's not just you and it's not a coincidence. They're tantalized by food smells way before they can eat it, they've been getting the flavors you eat in your amniotic fluid and in your milk all along.

You don't need to let your doctor perform cervical checks until you're in labor, unless there are signs of an incompetent cervix. It doesn't predict how soon you will go into labor, it only risks introducing bacteria and creating a problem. Plus, many OBs will want to do a stretch and sweep to try to put you into labor starting at your "due date" like it means something. They're risking rupturing your waters and forcing you into an likely c-section when everything is perfectly fine the way it is.
